findings.consequence: The runner can exit 0 with status complete beyond the registered 600-second budget. Artifact hashing time is omitted from reported total wall time. The separate 10-second reserve covers owned-group cleanup; it does not authorize unmetered normal final verification, receipts, or output hashing.
findings.finding: The last deadline decision compares the earlier execution_end timestamp. The supervisor closes its guard before final verification, writes run-result.json, then hashes all output files outside the guarded try/finally. No current-time check protects successful finalization. actual_total_wall_seconds is captured before run-result serialization and all artifact hashing.
findings.required_resolution: Keep all non-cleanup finalization within the original absolute deadline. If finalization crosses it, preserve failed partial evidence and return failure. Record elapsed time through final receipt/manifest work and keep cleanup time separate. Do not extend or relax any registered limit.
findings.retained_test_gap: test_harness.py:552-610 injects immediate failure into a dummy supervisor with a replacement guard. It does not exercise a successful near-deadline exit followed by slow finalization.
findings.title: Finalization can exceed the 600-second budget and still return complete
findings.trigger: A successful worker exits just before the deadline, then sampler shutdown, final input verification, receipt writing, or artifact hashing crosses the deadline.

findings.consequence: Remaining owned processes may still write inherited logs while they are hashed. The failure evidence can claim a stable artifact manifest without establishing all owned writers have stopped. This contradicts prepare_receipts.py:133 and the retained implementation limitation.
findings.finding: Cleanup correctly marks the run failed, but manifest publication checks only process.poll() is None. A dead leader with an unproven or nonempty owned group passes that check and receives artifact-manifest.json.
findings.required_resolution: Require both a reaped leader and positively established group_empty before publishing a stable manifest. Otherwise retain partial artifacts with artifact-manifest-unavailable.json. Keep the run failed and preserve cleanup errors.
findings.retained_test_gap: The retained dummy cleanup tests establish normal leader/group disappearance. They do not feed a reaped leader with group_empty false into supervisor finalization.
findings.title: A nonempty owned group still receives a supposedly stable artifact manifest
findings.trigger: The leader is reaped but stop_owned reports group_empty false, including a surviving descendant or inability to prove group absence.

review_synthetic_probes.interpretation: These probes demonstrate source control flow under declared synthetic conditions. They are not real-worker, operating-system cleanup, MPS, gameplay, resource-use, or campaign measurements.
review_synthetic_probes.method: Import only the frozen runner with importlib. Call its actual supervise function using in-memory output streams, fake Popen/stop_owned, a fixture protocol/manifest/lease and a controllable monotonic clock. Patch all persistence to an in-memory collector. No subprocess is created. No real campaign output or fixture file is written. Replacing the guard isolates finalization; the fixture clock remains before deadline during all normal checks.

source_review_observations.result: No static import-root blocker found. Runner ROOT resolves to source-snapshot; worker prepends capsule/python. Frozen identity.read_protocol resolves its registered protocol inside the capsule. The production ledger and python/.venv interpreter remain external. Runtime fields and exact native extension import path are checked in the worker. Existing training Guard/check_budget are not weakened or invoked.

The reader limits inputs to protocol-pinned checkpoint bytes, uses weights_only=True with the same narrow NumPy safe globals as prior inspect_checkpoints.py, checks complete-update/tag/counter/semantic identity and state shapes/dtypes/finite values, and loads model weights only. No optimizer/RNG/episode restore, checkpoint creation, eligibility mutation, or training call found.

The source preserves 64 independent B1 environments, direct D seeds, original D2 config, K4/cap18000, sorted shrinking alive batches, and no resets/fillers. Controls index completion-order saved rows by seed/index and compare all nine original fields. Entry and phase96 checks occur before any sampled evaluation; phase104 is a new baseline. Order contains exactly 12 groups / 768 episodes.

MPS Categorical uses real logits. Controller seeds are set once per sampled checkpoint/replicate after model loading. Full float32 teacher eval/no_grad and torch four-thread/no-fallback checks remain. Actual probabilities9, chosen/argmax actions, entropy and margin stream per decision. CPU transfers of completed outputs synchronize the data used before native steps; no real MPS execution was performed to verify timing or behavior.

Statistics first average three controller replicates within each seed, then bootstrap 64 paired clusters with 10000 draws and fixed seed764002. Shared indices span metrics. Primary phase104, secondary entry/phase96, margins100 alive frames / 1 score and mixed_or_inconclusive criteria match the registered protocol.

Observation presence is context only and death_cause remains UNKNOWN. Startup native updates7 and native counter420 are distinguished from wrapper frames. First visibility is explicitly observed at K4 boundaries, not raw activation or killer attribution.

Separate inference-only lease, sampled RSS/self peak/MPS guards and boundary deadline checks exist. Outer supervisor owns a new-session worker and cleanup targets its process group. No demonstrated steady-state hash/cadence blocker from the read-only measurements below. Finalization has the two reported defects.
